<reason>CON won by holding PRO to its burden: show what mandatory permission adds beyond enforceable upstream duties. PRO's timing/irreversibility default was strong, but CON answered that risk-based rules can require independent verification, evidence submission, and pre-release blocking, and exposed symmetry on vague standards and that PRO's provisional deployment on missed deadlines concedes safeguards can bind without completed clearance, plus asymmetric delay cost to challengers.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 A2-turn on the missed-deadline concession was decisive: if staged monitoring suffices when the authority is late, completed approval is not what makes prevention possible, undercutting PRO's gate-makes-tools-binding claim.</best_rebuttal>
